% The NAIVE conversion: class swapped, \frametitle/\framesubtitle left as they
% were. This is what a careful-looking conversion produces if nobody knows about
% C-FRAMESUBTITLE, and it is the deck this fixture exists to rule out.
%
% It compiles, exit 0, one page, Tagged: yes, and the word "Quiz" is absent from
% the PDF. assert-naive.sh asserts that absence, so the assertions on before.tex
% and after.tex are not vacuous: they check a property that demonstrably CAN be
% lost.
%
% If assert-naive.sh ever fails, ltx-talk has started typesetting the subtitle.
% That is the "revisit when" of the catalogue entry, and the runner reports it as
% advisory rather than failing the build.
\DocumentMetadata{lang=en, pdfversion=2.0, pdfstandard={a-4,ua-2}, tagging=on}
\documentclass{ltx-talk}

\begin{document}
\begin{frame}[vertical-alignment=center]
\frametitle{Constraint Satisfaction}
\framesubtitle{Quiz}
Body text.
\end{frame}
\end{document}
